title: Adversarial Inception Backdoor Attacks against Reinforcement Learning
page_convention: 1-based PDF pages; printed paper pages unless explicitly stated otherwise
summary: A finite exact construction gives V_M'(b)=15/16<1=V_M(b), contradicting Lemma 2 and its identity-remapping base case under the explicitly stated, source-supported reward-history interpretation. Eq52's substitution has residual -1/8. Separate local defects affect Eq1 normalization and a current-release rollout predecessor index.
supported_impact: Major invalid derivation supporting the central stealth guarantee. No direct refutation of Theorem 2's final optimality biconditional and no demonstrated failure of historical empirical scores.

problems.title: Consecutive poisoned states break the value-preservation derivation

original_claim.location: Main p6 Lemma2; Appendix A1.4 p16, base case and Eqs48–55, especially Eq52; Theorem2 dependence in Appendix A1.5 p18
original_claim.text: For all benign states and policies, V_pi^M'(s)>=V_pi^M(s); the identity-remapping base case claims equality.

assumptions: Finite benign states {low,b,high}, two actions {target,non-target}, deterministic self loops under either action; disjoint bijective poisoned copy.
Complete benign reward function R(s,a,s')=r(s'), with r(low)=0, r(b)=1/2, r(high)=1, including impossible cross-component transitions. Extrema are attained on actual self loops.
beta=gamma=1/2; policy always non-target, so phi argmax is never used on policy.
Grant normalized Eq10 full transition kernel in place of doubly weighted Eq1; grant benign successor pullback when R is called on a poisoned successor.
Use prior-reward domain [0,1] explicitly assumed by Eq15, not literal unrestricted reals.
Use the forward-consistent incoming reward for future tau in the benign-to-poison correction; original incoming and corrected received incoming readings agree here.

Entry rewards 0,3/4,1 satisfy c=r+gamma[r-tau(non-target,r,c)]. All 72 state/action/successor triples satisfy the reward bound for every admissible prior reward; endpoint enumeration is supported by monotonicity, not a finite-grid-only claim.

Central operative previous-reward histories {0,1/2,3/4} are closed and yield tau=0. If initial distribution is needed, uniform benign states makes both original extrema occur with positive probability.
problems.check: Exact Fraction solution of the two-state Bellman system with P rows (1/2,1/2) and rewards (1/2,3/4;0,0) gives (15/16,5/16). Both residuals are zero. Eq52's asserted Q_poison=Q_benign+tau-r gives 7/16 instead of 5/16. Parent separately checked all 72 complete reward-function triples at endpoints 0,1 and the algebraic interval bound.
problems.result: Lemma2's nondecrease and the identity base-case equality fail under the stated admissible-history interpretation; Eq52 residual is -1/8.
counterevidence: Eq7 is retained as a premise; the final destination-based off-support completion meets it on all state/action/successor triples for admissible prior rewards.

Literal Eq11/12 real domains remain unbounded: tau(target,1/2,-1)=-3/2 and tau(non-target,1/2,2)=5/2. This domain inconsistency is distinct; the counterexample is not claimed to satisfy that unrestricted specification.

The dot arguments in Eq12 are not fully specified. The report states the source-supported forward-incoming interpretation rather than claiming every possible interpretation has the same counterexample.
Consecutive poisoned states are explicitly allowed by Eq10. Excluding them changes the transition construction.

Algorithm1 and the practical release correct the preceding transition even when poisoned and use a stronger practical reward perturbation. The formal example is not evidence of empirical Q-Incept failure.
The theorem's policy-dependent construction requires a separate argument to refute its final optimality biconditional; this report claims a false supporting lemma and invalid proof dependency only.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem2's forward proof on p18 explicitly uses Lemmas1 and2. Main abstract, §4.3 and conclusion make bounded-reward attack-success/stealth guarantees central. A demonstrated invalid supporting derivation supports Major without requiring empirical-score loss or whole-paper collapse.
problems.impact: Major, scoped to the published value-preservation derivation under stated semantics; historical empirical impact unresolved.

correction.statement: No general theorem repair is certified. Adding reward1/4 to p_b->p_b restores v=1,w=1/2 only in the finite central example.
correction.verification: Local diagnostic checked exactly; globally bounded/history-consistent construction and optimality proof remain open.

problems.revision_note: Earlier auxiliary source-based off-support reward completion is retained as a historical candidate and superseded by the destination-based completion. Earlier checks established reachable-history bounds only; new checks supply the all-triple admissible-domain result.

problems.title: The formal transition constraint weights the mixture twice

original_claim.location: Main §3 p2 Eq1; main §4.2 p5 Eq10
original_claim.text: Eq1 applies coefficients (1-beta),beta to T' entries even though Eq10 defines T' as the already weighted full kernel.

assumptions: S and Sp are disjoint; delta is bijective; T and T' are stochastic rows; beta lies strictly between0 and1.
problems.check: Summing Eq1 gives (1-beta)P_B+beta P_P=1 with P_B+P_P=1, impossible since the left side is at most max(beta,1-beta)<1. At beta1/2 Eq10 row(1/2,1/2) gives Eq1 lhs1/2 instead of1.
problems.result: The literal constraint is inconsistent with the full-kernel definition.
counterevidence: The prose and Eq10 make the intended mixture clear; unweighted aggregation repairs the local normalization.
Branch-conditional interpretation would require distinct notation and conflicts with the actual Eq10 entries.
P1 grants the local repair; no empirical impossibility is inferred.
problems.core_dependency: Local formal-definition defect; the larger Major derivation finding is independently demonstrated after this repair.

correction.statement: Use T'(s'|a,s)+T'(delta(s')|a,s)=T(s'|a,s) for the full kernel, and synchronize subsequent expansions.
correction.verification: Aggregate row normalization checked analytically and exactly at beta1/2; this does not repair P1.

problems.title: The released predecessor correction wraps to a future rollout step at index zero

original_claim.location: Paper p6 Algorithm1 predecessor compensation; released adversary/OuterLoop.py85–100,140–150; ppo.py241–248
original_claim.text: The practical compensation modifies the preceding reward, but the release directly indexes rewards[index-1] on the current chronological slice.

assumptions: Attack enabled, caller asr<1 and sampling budget allow selection.
Finite categorical logits give index0 positive probability, and a positive selected score leads to the target action.
Cached empirical L=0,U=1 have already been observed in earlier data; a first constant batch alone would not establish them.
Three chronological rewards all1/2 and gamma1/2; selected index0.
problems.check: The branch sets current reward to1 and writes max(0,1/2-(1/2)(1-1/2))=1/4 to rewards[-1], the final future step of the slice.
problems.result: A concrete conditional temporal-index error in the pinned release.
counterevidence: No historical logs show whether the branch occurred or changed ASR/benign return.
Frequency depends on selection and rollout length; neither removes the branch semantics.
Pinned current release is not established as the historical experimental executable.
problems.core_dependency: Local released preprocessing branch; no material core empirical effect established.
problems.impact: Minor current-release defect; historical occurrence and empirical impact Needs Evidence.

correction.statement: Define and retain the actual preceding transition across rollout/episode boundaries; do not substitute the final future entry.
correction.verification: No source modification or general implementation repair performed; exact branch arithmetic only.
